definitions.explanation: The traditional process of making mochi by pounding steamed glutinous rice with a large wooden mallet in a mortar. A festive activity associated with the New Year season.

examples.japanese: {年末|ねんまつ}に{餅|もち}つきをした。
examples.english: We did mochi pounding at the end of the year.

examples.japanese: {町内|ちょうない}{会|かい}で{餅|もち}つき{大会|たいかい}が{開|ひら}かれた。
examples.english: A mochi-pounding event was held by the neighborhood association.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちは{初|はじ}めての{餅|もち}つき{体験|たいけん}に{大|おお}はしゃぎだった。
examples.english: The children were thrilled by their first mochi-pounding experience.

notes:
A traditional New Year preparation activity. Steamed {餅米|もちごめ} (glutinous rice) is placed in an {臼|うす} (mortar) and pounded with a {杵|きね} (wooden mallet). One person pounds while another turns and wets the rice — this teamwork is called {合|あ}いの{手|て}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {餅|もち}つきをする (to pound mochi)
- {餅|もち}つき{大会|たいかい} (mochi-pounding event)
- {餅|もち}つき{体験|たいけん} (mochi-pounding experience)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditionally done around December 28 or 30 for New Year preparations. Pounding on the 29th is avoided because 29 can be read as {苦|く} (suffering). Community {餅|もち}つき events remain popular, especially for children.
